title: Evaluation & routing rubric for hosted chat/streaming/tool-call feature intake
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Goal: Create a reproducible intake rubric and routing rules for hosted API feature requests that involve chat, streaming, tool/function calling, and structured outputs from enterprise customers.

Scope:
- Define signal weighting (security, SLA, data residency, latency impact, implementation complexity, customer revenue) for prioritization.
- Produce routing rules (self-serve backlog, PM triage, sales-assisted, expedite to Dedicated/Private workstreams).
- Produce a checklist for engineering readiness (API compatibility, streaming semantics, function schema, fallback policies).

Acceptance criteria:
- Published rubric doc in Confluence with scoring examples for 10 sample customer requests.
- Triage routing flow implemented as a lightweight Airtable/Notion view and a templated Linear workflow.
- Pilot with 3 enterprise incoming requests; measure lead time and correctness of routing.

Trade-offs:
- Heavier scoring improves precision but increases triage latency; propose triage automation heuristics for low-signal requests.
- Conservative security gating may push more work to Private/Dedicated which increases RFEs for infra.

Success metrics:
- Routing accuracy >= 85% (correct endpoint: hosted vs dedicated vs private vs require SSO/KMS) during pilot.
- Time from request to assigned owner <= 48h for enterprise signals.
- Reduction in back-and-forth clarifying questions by 30% on triaged tickets.

Next steps:
1) Draft rubric (this ticket).
2) PM + Solutions + Sales review (owner: Miguel).
3) Engineering feasibility sync (runtime, console, intake automation).
4) Pilot + iterate.

Stakeholders: Product (Asha), Solutions Engineering (Rajiv Anand), Sales AE (Lina Gomez), Runtime Eng (Sofia Petrov), Security (Daniel Brooks), Design (Yuna Kim).
